sections.kicker: Prepared for Bahia Hotel & Beach House by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Bahia has a name and a mood. The front door does not yet say what only Bahia is.
sections.keep: Your logo lockup, "Hotel & Beach House" under the wordmark. It gives the place a character before any photo loads.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.what: The headline closes on the hotel's own name.
pins.why: It asks the visitor to already know what Bahia is. A first-time guest in Los Cabos gets no reason to pick it over the resort next door.
pins.how: Name the one thing a stay here gives that the next hotel does not, then let the name follow.
pins.label: Your headline
pins.cost: Bahia gets compared on room rates, because the headline offers no other measure.

pins.area: Two photos split the hero, white beach umbrellas and a pool beside a balcony
pins.what: The hero shows a pool, umbrellas and a woman in a green dress at a table.
pins.why: Every beach hotel opens with these same props. Nothing in the image says Bahia, or Los Cabos, or why this house.
pins.how: Show the one view, room or ritual that exists only here.
pins.label: Your hero
pins.cost: Visitors cannot tell Bahia apart from the other photos in their search results.

pins.area: The logo lockup reads BAHIA with Hotel & Beach House Los Cabos beneath
pins.what: The logo lockup calls Bahia a beach house, not a hotel.
pins.why: It is the most distinctive idea on the page, a house you stay in. The rest of the site never builds on it.
pins.how: Carry the beach house idea into the words, rooms and photography.
pins.label: Your logo
pins.cost: The one word that sets Bahia apart stays a caption under the logo.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Bahia. I spent some time on your site. Three things stood out, and all three point the same way.
